warnings.why: Household consumption exceeding 100% of GDP is mathematically impossible in standard national accounting unless heavily distorted by massive unrecorded remittances or severe statistical discrepancies.
A value of 129% is implausibly high for a national aggregate under standard GDP accounting without severe economic collapse and data distortion.
At 114%, consumption exceeding total GDP points to severe data collection issues or severe distortion from conflict economies.
A value of 112% exceeds total GDP, indicating unreliable national accounts data following recent political and economic upheavals.
Consumption at 104% of GDP is extremely high, typically only explainable by massive foreign aid inflows treated improperly in consumption aggregates.
A value of 101% implies consumption outstrips total domestic production, which is structurally unsustainable without massive uncaptured transfers.
Consumption at 101% of GDP suggests data reporting errors or severe gaps in investment and export statistics.
At 19.5%, while Qatar has massive GDP due to LNG exports, such an extremely low consumption rate requires careful verification against national accounts.
